sent_subject: Fell View House: 10‑point conversion teardown (first 48‑hour fixes)
sent:
Maya —

You’re getting the clicks; the blockers are clarity (min‑stay/real rate by dates) and trust (reviews/flexibility) not living where people decide to search.

Here’s the 10‑point shortlist, ordered by speed to impact:

48‑hour fixes
1) Put “Most weekends: 2‑night minimum” visibly on the Rooms page and each room tile; repeat the note next to the date picker.
2) Move “Why book direct” perks to sit beside the date picker and the portal hand‑off; add “Flexible cancellation” in plain words there.
3) Add a reviews strip above the fold: 2–3 recent lines with source badges and a link to the source.
4) Change “From £129 BB” to “From £129 BB (typical midweek)” and swap the CTA on tiles to “View availability” to cue date‑first behaviour.

Two‑week tests
5) If your portal exposes it, surface live availability (and an indicative rate) on room tiles for selected dates; pre‑fill dates on click either way.
6) Show “Only X rooms left for your dates” and “Secure booking, free cancellation” next to the date picker; include your phone number there for last‑minute callers.
7) Booking flow friction: keep people in the same tab, preserve a clear “Back to rooms” link, keep dates pre‑filled, and show a simple progress indicator.

Page structure and UX
8) Room tiles: tighten hierarchy—name, sleeps, breakfast included, 2–3 hero amenities, then price; keep secondary details behind “More info.”
9) Calendar UX: grey out impossible single nights when a 2‑night minimum applies and explain the rule inline so it feels like guidance, not an error.
10) Mobile: compress the hero, make the date picker and CTAs thumb‑sized, and add a sticky “Book now” that carries selected dates across pages.

Measurement to prove it worked
- In your analytics, track a simple funnel: Availability search -> Room tile clicks -> Portal start -> Confirmation. Use it to read where fall‑off improves as you ship the fixes.

If you want, I can share wireframe examples for the room tiles, date picker block, and the reviews strip we’ve used with bookings‑led brands.
